requirements.requirement: Set up /srv/data so it is recoverable through filesystem snapshots
requirements.summary: Built a device-mapper snapshot-origin/snapshot pair (loopback-backed XFS origin at /dev/mapper/data-origin, COW snapshot device data-snap) providing real filesystem-snapshot capability for /srv/data, given no LVM/btrfs/package access on this RHEL 7.9 image. Verified via dmsetup ls/table and successful snapshot creation.

requirements.requirement: Modify /srv/data after the snapshot is captured
requirements.summary: app.conf corrupted, counter.txt changed, and an unexpected.txt added after data-snap was created; dmsetup status confirms COW blocks captured prior state (48/1048576 allocated).

requirements.requirement: Restore /srv/data to the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: Snapshot device mounted read-only and its checksums matched the pre-modification baseline exactly; /srv/data was then cleared and repopulated from the snapshot, with a post-restore sha256 diff against the original baseline showing an exact match (unexpected.txt removed, originals restored byte-for-byte).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart healthy baseline/boot id, restart ack, new boot id, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id fe422859-... and healthy checksummed data captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnection; node was unreachable during reboot then returned with new boot_id 4f22c5c7-...; post-restart state shows dm-origin device reattached via enabled systemd units, /srv/data automatically remounted, and checksums matching baseline exactly. Cross-checked against fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots, which show the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: node1's /srv/data was made snapshot-recoverable using a manually constructed device-mapper snapshot-origin/snapshot pair (the only viable mechanism given no LVM/btrfs/repo access), the directory was subsequently modified, and it was restored to the exact snapshot-captured content, verified by matching SHA-256 checksums before and after. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a full pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, differing post-restart boot_id, and confirmed recovery of the dm device, mount, and data integrity, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so native package-manager consistency cannot be independently confirmed, though this is unrelated to the task outcome.

The snapshot solution is a manually engineered device-mapper construct rather than a native LVM/btrfs snapshot, reflecting genuine platform constraints (no root-accessible package repos) rather than an implementation shortcut.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological command trace: initial discovery commands (os-release, df, lsblk, which lvs/vgs/pvs/btrfs) were read-only. The `yum install -y lvm2` attempts (cmd-b242140e0ba240d6, cmd-13426c50428d4dc4) failed (no root, then no enabled repos) and made no persistent state change — legitimate exploratory attempts to find a standard snapshot mechanism before falling back to device-mapper, not unnecessary mutations. All loopback devices, dm targets, mount points, and the temporary data-snap/mnt mount created during the exercise were either retained as the intended final persistent setup (data-origin, /srv/data mount, systemd units) or explicitly torn down afterward (cmd-f47b0a09ad964bed unmounts /mnt/data-snap, removes data-snap, detaches loop1). No abandoned services, failed units, or unsafe exposure were introduced; after-executor failed-services and listening-sockets checks show only expected reboot-driven PID/timestamp changes, no new listeners. A handful of small sha256/log files were left in /tmp as evidence artifacts, a low-severity, bounded residue.
